title: Build the Meridian Dataset
brief: Install the package and run notebooks 01, 02, 03 and 99 in order. Every one of the
Then read the data for twenty minutes. Open each table, read the column comments, and
run whatever occurs to you. Write down:
- three questions a business user might ask that this data could answer two
- any column whose meaning you had to guess
- the total value of assets Meridian manages, and how you decided which number
Keep the sheet. You come back to it in Module 4, and the gap between what you noticed
now and what you can name then is the point of the exercise.
The checks below confirm the dataset built correctly. They do not read your sheet.

checks.name: The twelve core objects exist
sql: SELECT count(*) >= 12 AS ok, concat(count(*), ' core objects') AS detail
checks.hint: Nine dimensions and three facts. Run notebooks 02 and 03.

checks.name: dim_date covers both fiscal years
sql: SELECT count(*) = 730 AS ok, concat(count(*), ' dates, expected 730') AS detail

checks.name: Reporting dates are month-ends, not every day
sql: SELECT count(*) = 24 AS ok, concat(count(*), ' reporting dates, expected 24') AS detail
checks.hint: 24 month-ends across two years. A reporting date is the last BUSINESS day.

checks.name: The fiscal year starts in October
sql: SELECT count(*) = 0 AS ok, concat(count(*), ' dates in the wrong fiscal year') AS detail
WHERE date_key BETWEEN DATE'2025-10-01' AND DATE'2026-09-30' AND fiscal_year <> 'FY2026'
checks.hint: FY2026 runs 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30. Calendar year is not fiscal year here.

checks.name: fct_aum_snapshot really is a daily snapshot
sql: concat(count(DISTINCT snapshot_date), ' distinct dates') AS detail
checks.hint: One row per account per day. This is the trap the whole course keeps returning to.

checks.name: Flows carry all six types, including exchanges
sql: concat(count(DISTINCT flow_type), ' flow types') AS detail
checks.hint: SUBSCRIPTION, REDEMPTION, EXCHANGE_IN, EXCHANGE_OUT, TRANSFER_IN, TRANSFER_OUT.

checks.name: Both asset-class hierarchies are present
sql: SELECT count(*) = 2 AS ok, concat(count(*), ' hierarchy columns') AS detail
checks.hint: Two ways to roll up the same assets. Module 7 is where you pick one.

checks.name: Portfolios and advisors generated deterministically
sql: concat((SELECT count(*) FROM {{CORE}}dim_portfolio), ' portfolios, expected 4500') AS detail
checks.hint: Values derive from hash() not rand(), so your data is byte-identical to everyone else's.

review: The sheet names three questions that the data answers two ways, with the reason.
The stated AUM total says which definition was chosen and why.
At least one guessed column is identified — there are several.
